evidence.ref: .warp/runcmd.py is a thin stdlib CLI over runlog.post_command (R5): warp answer/steer/abort <run-id> [text] post the matching command (answer, steer, abort) with the human's plain text as the payload to the target run's inbox, print the command id, and fail loud with a nonzero exit on an unknown run or empty required text (abort reason optional); it reimplements no inbox logic - it calls post_command, the same commands the R5 run loop drains at a safe checkpoint - and writes only through runlog. plugin/skills/run/SKILL.md documents the chat-surface procedure (an assistant, e.g. on Telegram, watches with warp status --json and issues these) and restates the requirement-change-must-commit rule so a chat answer never becomes hidden engineering truth.

a selftest block drives the CLI over a temporary runs root: answer, steer, and abort each land the correct kind and the exact supplied text as payload in the target run's inbox (three commands, no more), an empty answer/steer text is rejected, an unknown run exits nonzero and posts nothing, and main() happy path returns 0; non-tautological - a wrong-kind or fixed-empty-payload mutation turns the kind/payload assertions red; part of selftest 848 passed, 0 failed
